reviews.text: The Big Sick can confidently boast a self-evident punchline that lasts for over two hours and never runs out of the funny or the surprising.
reviews.author: Don Shanahan

reviews.text: Every laugh is full and genuine, and so are the (good) tears you inevitably will cry.
reviews.author: Patricia Karounos

reviews.text: The characters are funny, but not too funny, the stakes seem real, and you can tell that everyone really cares about each other.
reviews.author: Fletcher Powell

reviews.text: The Big Sick feels authentic yet familiar, endearing and consistently funny - a curious mix that provides a real-life example of how Nanjiani and Gordon's life together imitates art.
reviews.author: Brian Eggert

reviews.text: The Big Sick falls under one of my favorite criteria in film watching  unexpected surprises.
reviews.author: David Gonzalez

reviews.text: An utter delight that mines the right kinds of humor, drama, and romance out of such a personal story.
reviews.author: Drew Dietsch

reviews.text: Generously laced with wit and wisdom.
reviews.author: Matt Brunson

reviews.text: There's a lot of blackness there from which to find humour and 'The Big Sick' mines enormous amounts.
reviews.author: Olly Richards

reviews.text: A crowd-pleaser that still feels personal and intimate.
reviews.author: Richard Crouse

reviews.text: The story beats may be traditional but the sensibility, and especially the jokes, are of the moment.
reviews.author: David Bax

reviews.text: Refreshingly, it's almost as if the film wasn't designed to be a comedy; laughs are conjured naturally from everyday situations and uncomfortable interactions.
reviews.author: Mike Massie

reviews.text: Kumail Nanjiani and Emily Gordon's real-life love story serves as inspiration for the film that put romantic comedies back on the map.
reviews.author: Film Companion Staff

reviews.text: Kumail Nanjiani, Zoe Kazan, Ray Ramano and Holly Hunter are so funny that they yank the rom-com genre right out of a coma.
reviews.author: Jason Fraley

reviews.text: The Big Sick is everything a good romantic comedy should be. It's funny, sweet, smart, emotional and, even more amazing, it's true.
reviews.author: Damond Fudge

reviews.text: No matter how dark the reality is, there's always a reason to smile here. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Ricardo Gallegos

reviews.text: In some ways this love story feels old-fashioned - but it is also modern, by touching on Islamophobia. Nanjiani playing himself provides integrity and while there is high drama or perfect comedic timing at times, it is character-driven at its core.
reviews.author: Fiona Underhill

reviews.text: I really liked this movie.
reviews.author: Andrew Galdi

reviews.text: I loved this movie. It was fabulous.
reviews.author: Avaryl Halley

reviews.text: The film is equal parts heartwarming and heartbreaking, and the entire package is completely entertaining thanks in large part to the eclectic and flawless cast.
reviews.author: Steven Prokopy

reviews.text: ...a universality that should prove broad enough for even the most close-minded of viewers...
reviews.author: Elissa Suh

reviews.text: The Big Sick is so funny, so smart, so heartfelt that it demands to be seen.
reviews.author: Tim Brennan

reviews.text: This is a comedy with real-life stakes that's not about being cruel to anyone. It's also a little shaggy and loose, which is excusable because the characters are so fun to be around.
reviews.author: Chris McCoy

reviews.text: If you're in the mood for a heartwarming romantic drama which manages to tackle some heavy themes, then The Big Sick might be right up your alley. Just don't expect Mamma Mia and you'll have a great time.
reviews.author: Kieran McLoone

reviews.text: It cleanses the palate, boosts your spirits and makes your veins pulse with laughter, love and life.
reviews.author: Kate Rodger

reviews.text: It is one of the most charming and fun movies of 2017. [Full Review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Juan Luis Caviaro

reviews.text: Ray Romano and Holly Hunter as Emily's parents are the kinds of supporting performances that feel so much larger than they are because they control every minute of screen time they have.
reviews.author: Karl Delossantos

reviews.text: The sincerity of the tale and the unexpected success of Nanjiani as the male lead make The Big Sick tantalizing and infectiously (pun intended) appealing.
reviews.author: Allison Rose

reviews.text: The Big Sick is that rare film that reminds us, through both wry humor and understated poignancy, that life's most meaningful moments often occur when we veer off script.
reviews.author: Josh Goller

reviews.text: By no means a perfect film, this often clunky and clumsy charmer is a love letter to our commonality; it is simultaneously an intimate story of romance and a mass-appeal to remember that we are all defined by variations on the same few themes.
reviews.author: Ryan Syrek

reviews.text: The film's end leaves us with the promise of that culture clash, which seems more exciting than its altogether too sanguine resolution. The Big Sick is not that film. But the congenial one we do get will do.
reviews.author: Andrew Kendall

reviews.text: The Big Sick is a rare romantic comedy that feels genuine and real in a way most movies based on true stories fail to be.
reviews.author: Kaitlyn Booth

reviews.text: I loved all the supporting performances but I honestly think Ray Ramano and Holly Hunter are nomination worthy as Emily's parents.
reviews.author: Rachel Wagner

reviews.text: The bland, impersonal music and cinematography may not inspire, yet The Big Sick is a welcome addition to cinema's ongoing exploration of identity politics in contemporary America.
reviews.author: Rachel Brook

reviews.text: It's a staid premise no doubt: boy meets girl but something obviously stands in the way of their true love. But the film's genuinely funny humour moors its journey, transporting it through familiar terrain.
reviews.author: Deborah Cornelious

reviews.text: The Big Sick takes on some pretty big themes. Luckily, the talent involved both behind the camera and in front of it is able to not only explore those themes, but to incorporate them both honestly and humorously.
reviews.author: Allen Adams

reviews.text: The Big Sick hits all the right notes at all the right times. It's funny and silly when it needs to be. It's romantic and cute at the right moments. And it sprinkles the drama and realism throughout.
reviews.author: Doug Jamieson

reviews.text: What follows is an off-beat romance that constantly bucks against rom-com conventions.
reviews.author: Marisa Carpico

reviews.text: A fine movie that's anchored by great performances and story that you can't help but fall into.
reviews.author: Matt Hudson

reviews.text: There are certain movies that are so intensely personal, so fiercely credible that there's no question they are based on true stories. The Big Sick feels authentic because it is authentic.
reviews.author: Louisa Moore

reviews.text: The Big Sick is one of the most honest, straightforward, quality pieces of American cinema this decade.
reviews.author: Matt Ward

reviews.text: this is a real American story about cultures clashing and finding a common ground. [Emily] Gordon and [Kumail] Nanjiani's writing shows that we as Americans have many more similarities than we realize; all we have to do is dig deeper.
reviews.author: James Clay

reviews.text: The Big Sick perfectly captures the Millennial experience, along with all the cultural tensions that come with changing demographics.
reviews.author: Li Lai

reviews.text: The Big Sick is hilarious, heartbreaking, and heartwarming all at the same time.
reviews.author: Kent Garrison

reviews.text: It may seem like an incredibly simple romantic comedy on paper, but The Big Sick succeeds by avoiding all the usual rom com traps and hones in on the emotional content.
reviews.author: Jennifer Heaton

reviews.text: It has a strong script that delivers the promised comedy, a rare phenomenon. The characters are relatable and refreshingly unfilmy. Kumail comes through as a writer, as an actor and as a comedian.
reviews.author: Pooja Pande

reviews.text: Movies like The Big Sick don't come around that often.
reviews.author: Sean Mulvihill

reviews.text: The Big Sick is the kind of film that can cause tears from both joy and pain in the same scene -- a lovely blend of drama and laughs that strikes just the right balance.
reviews.author: Micheal Compton

reviews.text: It deals love, death, faith, country, family, friendship and career in a way that's never sentimental, though I defy you to get to the end without shedding a tear.
reviews.author: Alexa Dalby

reviews.text: In a very real sense, you'll laugh and you'll cry in equal measure.
reviews.author: Joey Magidson

reviews.text: The Big Sick will open your eyes to a culture many have never witnessed and a couple that is more mainstream than Hollywood would typically care to admit.
reviews.author: Aaron Peterson

reviews.text: There is something in that ungainly mixture of gratification and denial that makes The Big Sick work so well in its latter half. If it does not begin on the strongest of legs, it makes sure to have its ending count.
reviews.author: Tomas Trussow

reviews.text: Between the stellar cast, likable characters and the engaging script, there is plenty here to like.
reviews.author: Kimberly Pierce

reviews.text: Isn't just a romantic comedy that defines its genre but a movie that defines the art of screenwriting and what romance stories should be.
reviews.author: Rendy Jones

reviews.text: Happily, The Big Sick makes a welcome recovery from all these potential setbacks to be that rare thing, a genuinely feelgood comedy centred around an absolute bummer of an event.
reviews.author: Alison Rowat

reviews.text: This film is actually one of the year's best so far. If you want to know what budding young relationships look like in America these days, this is the most pleasurable tutorial you'll ever see.
reviews.author: Lisa Johnson Mandell

reviews.text: Despite the seemingly downer subject matter, The Big Sick is indeed very funny and moving, if slightly bloated.
reviews.author: Glenn Heath Jr.

reviews.text: I left The Big Sick feeling charmed, even though I could probably count the amount of times I laughed on one hand.
reviews.author: Alistair Ryder

reviews.text: The film's formula is evocative of feelings, without losing the internal tragedy and without trivializing anything. [Full Review in Spanish]
reviews.author: William Venegas

reviews.text: The ultimate message is that, once we find love, vows are worth both taking and keeping.
reviews.author: Megan Basham

reviews.text: The Big Sick is that rarest of romantic comedies, in that it's both funny (often hilariously so) and poignant while still allowing its characters to grow and develop despite the constraints of the genre.
reviews.author: Pete Vonder Haar

reviews.text: It's a pity that "The Big Sick" didn't get released in Peruvian theatres; I'm sure people looking for something different, entertaining, intelligent and deeply personal would have enjoyed it. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Sebastian Zavala Kahn

reviews.text: It's been a long time since this genre found a crowd-pleaser that is also so intelligent. [Full Review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Diego Batlle

reviews.text: ... Kumail's scenes with his parents, his brother and his sister-in-law are the best in the film. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Gaspar Zimerman

reviews.text: A success like The Big Sick really needs to be celebrated, if only to prove that there ARE audiences out there for good, small, well-told stories of love and family, and that the American moviegoing public hasn't completely abandoned quality film.
reviews.author: Joe Reid

reviews.text: The Big Sick stars Nanjiani as himself (or a version thereof), joined by Zoe Kazan (Ruby Sparks) as Emily. Together they have a genuinely sweet chemistry.
reviews.author: Christopher Llewellyn Reed

reviews.text: The Big Sick is offering hope that comedy isn't dead at the box office.
reviews.author: Carl Kozlowski

reviews.text: Working with director Michael Showalter and producer Judd Apatow, Nanjiani and Gordon have crafted a deft and appearling film that addresses subjects ranging from cultural change to the unhappy lot of the Uber driver.
reviews.author: Michael Bonner

reviews.text: What The Big Sick ends up accomplishing, is -- in my mind -- perfect romantic comedy.
reviews.author: Evan Romano

reviews.text: It's a hybridized rom-com that is this summer's winning feature, equal parts funny, cringey, heartwarming and wise (and you might even shed a tear or two).
reviews.author: Al Hoff

reviews.text: Nanjiani expertly underplays the comedy but the true MVPs are the parents on all sides: Bollywood legend Anupam Kher as Nanjiani's taciturn father and Holly Hunter as Emily's mother.
reviews.author: Eli Glasner

reviews.text: With its honesty and adroit mix of drama and dark humor, "The Big Sick" breathes new life into the commercial contemporary romantic comedy. It's a genuine crowd-pleaser with substance.
reviews.author: Loren King

reviews.text: It's a joy to watch two "real people" (albeit unusually witty, clever and attractive "real people") fall in and out and back in love. And, it's particularly satisfying that their mothers have so much to do with it.
reviews.author: Alexandra MacAaron

reviews.text: A Terms of Endearment for the Trainwreck era.
reviews.author: Matt Patches

reviews.text: The Big Sick is One of 2017's Best Films
reviews.author: Danielle Solzman

reviews.text: The Big Sick is a simple and effective story... [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Mariana Fernández

reviews.text: To the sound of Vampire Weekend and being irresistibly charming, The Big Sick dispenses with any classic structure... [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Andrea G. Bermejo

reviews.text: Indeed, the Allenian influence is omnipresent in this romantic comedy... [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Ernesto Diezmartinez

reviews.text: [There's] an appreciable balance between uninhibited comedy and a melancholy tone. [Full Review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Alberto Bermejo

reviews.text: Tender, bittersweet and funny, a well-told, simple story can achieve a lot. [Full Review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Carlos Díaz Reyes

reviews.text: ... nonethelss has a certain spontaneity, a certain freshness, a certain purity, a certain grace. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Carlos Boyero

reviews.text: ... its success - and what we appreciate in a time flooded with formulas and little innovation - is that it does not follow any traditional formula. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Jorge Iván Morales

reviews.text: [The Big Sick has the] gives an injection of adrenaline to a genre that has been in a coma for a long time. [Full Review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Roger Salvans

reviews.text: [The Big Sick] has much humor and love, but not in the doses or formats that you'd expect. Fortunately. [Full Review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Manuel Piñón

reviews.text: As far as performances go, Ray and Holly lead the way; Anupam Kher is adept and Kumail with his mostly-comic expressions passes muster.
reviews.author: Meena Iyer

reviews.text: An effortlessly great film is born in the process. This is the best Judd Apatow movie and it wasn't even directed by Apatow
reviews.author: Jordan Ruimy

reviews.text: ... gives us a conciliatory message on the understanding between cultures, in times much in need of them. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: José Martín

reviews.text: There is a real dramatic streak throughout the film, but its real strength lies in being at once uproariously funny and endlessly charming.
reviews.author: Rob Dean

reviews.text: This multicultural romance succeeds because the filmmakers have avoided the cultural clichés that usually dog the genre.
reviews.author: Richard James Havis

reviews.text: ... The Big Sick tells a heart-warming tale of how the couple go through the ups and downs brought about by their cultural differences.
reviews.author: Charmaine Soh

reviews.text: Like Apatow's best, it is filled with quirkiness, pathos, drama - there are stakes involved. And the story like real life - and in this case, it was real life - has its ups and downs.
reviews.author: Rob Lowman

reviews.text: The Big Sick is a brilliant film. It's funny and warm, and for anyone who has married across differing cultures, very, very real.
reviews.author: Keeva Stratton

reviews.text: The Big Sick signals the arrival of a new prince in the comic kingdom.
reviews.author: tt stern-enzi

reviews.text: The acting is very good and the story (co-written by Emily V. Gordon) is highly original. As a bonus, it is based on a true story which is pretty upbeat, even though this edgy movie is less so.
reviews.author: Robert Roten

reviews.text: There's nothing quite like The Big Sick out there, and particularly in these times, there's nothing like a gentle reminder that even across vast differences in cultural values and beliefs, love can conquer all.
reviews.author: Nathaniel Rogers

reviews.text: The Big Sick proceeds into a palpably puffed-up midsection that's rife with overlong sequences and somewhat needless digressions...
reviews.author: David Nusair

reviews.text: A textured, multifaceted example of rom-coms at their very best.
reviews.author: Sarah Ward

reviews.text: Seldom do films achieve the delicate balance of humor and serious commentary. Kudos, then, to The Big Sick, a funny, sweet character study steeped in cultural issues.
reviews.author: Diane Carson

reviews.text: The Big Sick comes to life just fine. But it's a little unsettling to consider that what might turn out to be the best romantic comedy of the year depends so heavily on a girlfriend in a coma.
reviews.author: Jesse Hassenger

reviews.text: It's exceedingly amusing in a light, affable register, even as it gets increasingly grey and grim in terms of the emotional states it depicts.
reviews.author: Tim Brayton

reviews.text: Cozy but not cloying; funny without trying too hard.
reviews.author: Brian Gibson

reviews.text: Clearly, The Big Sick has its roots in autobiography -- which, after all, may be the basis of some of our best comedies.
reviews.author: Robert Denerstein

reviews.text: The film does push against most of the easy rom-com cliches to deliver a satisfying adult comedy. One value it does share with most American comedies is how its veneer of humour packages a set of values that are chiefly conservative and very American.
reviews.author: Jim Schembri

reviews.text: An intelligent film that offers a blend of real-life material and genre conventions.
reviews.author: Uri Klein

reviews.text: The Big Sick has a true and beating heart, and it adds up to a sweet and wonderful romance
reviews.author: Karen Gordon

reviews.text: Without overemphasising either the laughs or the emotion, The Big Sick is a romantic comedy that feels genuine.
reviews.author: Alex Doenau

reviews.text: Utterly refreshing, like a big bowl of ice cream after a serving of spicy food.
reviews.author: Matt Neal

reviews.text: What sets the film apart is an oddness that could only have sprung from real life. That and sincerity, compassion, humanity.
reviews.author: Donald Clarke

reviews.text: Both the script and the direction, from Michael Showalter, move with such pleasing assurance, held aloft by warm currents of banter backstage and at the dinner table, that you don't notice the deceptions that Kumail practises in the name of deference.
reviews.author: Craig Mathieson

reviews.text: After a slow start, the film gradually accumulates funny and surprising details, many of them surely drawn directly from life.
reviews.author: Jake Wilson

reviews.text: It may be rather long for a romantic comedy, but this film has such a strikingly original script that it grabs hold and never lets go.
reviews.author: Rich Cline

reviews.text: The Big Sick gives us a love to aspire to, and when you're dating while sick sometimes you need to be reminded that -- as cheesy as it is -- love conquers all.
reviews.author: Kylie Maslen

reviews.text: Very charming and certainly close to the bone.
reviews.author: David 'Mad Dog' Bradley

reviews.text: A refreshingly entertaining film with a hell of a lot of heart.
reviews.author: Steve Newall

reviews.text: The secret sauce flavouring this wonderful movie ... [is that] it's sincere ... This beautiful film will appeal to all, but it is built by grown-ups, and not afraid to wear its intelligence proudly.
reviews.author: CJ Johnson

reviews.text: The Big Sick is so funny and so heartfelt it leaves the audience delighted, while expertly examining romance, relationships and the importance of family.
reviews.author: Tim Appelo

reviews.text: A timeless and timely look at love in all of its complicated forms, The Big Sick also examines parental sacrifice and the immigrant's dilemma of assimilation versus tradition.
reviews.author: James Croot

reviews.text: Nanjiani and Gordon's sharp, intuitive scripting has a lot to say about modern love, age-old prejudices and the simple act of being there for someone who doesn't even know you're there.
reviews.author: Leigh Paatsch

reviews.text: A very funny and authentic film, with effective drama that gives it weight but doesn't weigh it down.
reviews.author: Eric D. Snider

reviews.text: The film's message - that cultures are different but can coexist peacefully - is a welcome one in these riven times.
reviews.author: Naman Ramachandran

reviews.text: This is the kind of rom-com anyone can get behind - even the manliest of Vin Diesel-watching men - because there's nothing more universal than falling in love.
reviews.author: Wenlei Ma

reviews.text: [A] very special movie, and one I was happy to live inside of 124 minutes.
reviews.author: Simon Miraudo

reviews.text: At 125 minutes, it's a grind that never finds an equilibrium between feel-good comedy and incisive slice of life. And it's never quite funny enough.
reviews.author: J. Olson

reviews.text: Nanjiani is a wonderful screen presence, combining George Clooney good looks with a kind of soft-spoken gormlessness.
reviews.author: Nick Dent

reviews.text: Nanjiani and Kazan are joined by a darling supporting cast that includes Holly Hunter and Ray Romano. And yes, the ending will very much leave you with "all the feels", as the kids say today.
reviews.author: Hilary A White

reviews.text: It has moments that are deeply serious, and some that are deeply funny, but it never truly commits to those dramatic peaks and valleys.
reviews.author: John Serba

reviews.text: A comedy with heart and soul to spare.
reviews.author: Mark Kermode

reviews.text: Many films have been made about cross-cultural relationships but The Big Sick will win over most in the audience with its delicately balanced mix of comedy and authenticity.
reviews.author: Matthew Toomey

reviews.text: The originality here, though, is in the cultural detail, and the earthy likeability of the two leads.
reviews.author: Paul Whitington

reviews.text: The Big Sick is messy and complex in a fantastic way, exuding a deeply-felt empathy for all its charming characters.
reviews.author: Roe McDermott

reviews.text: The Big Sick is an enchanting film with a terrible title. Don't be put off by it.
reviews.author: Jasper Rees

reviews.text: We're aways off awards season, but it would be an awful pity if The Big Sick wasn't at the business end of things at the start of 2018.
reviews.author: Harry Guerin

reviews.text: These are real characters living real lives, and the humour -- much of it is extremely funny -- is rooted in this reality.
reviews.author: David Stratton

reviews.text: A rom-com for people who hate rom-coms. A painfully funny movie, full of enrapturing emotion that captures the glorious contradictions of all kinds of love.
reviews.author: MaryAnn Johanson

reviews.text: Watching this Judd Apatow-produced romcom is like clicking on a for-real YouTube clip of a kitten juggling spoons. Cute. Clever. No wonder The Big Sick has gone viral.
reviews.author: Charlotte O'Sullivan

reviews.text: Often laugh-out-loud funny, bravely fencing with interracial tensions in post-9/11 America.
reviews.author: Damon Wise

reviews.text: Donald Trump would surely hate it - and that has to be a good thing.
reviews.author: Matthew Turner

reviews.text: The film is a hoot. It's a hit. It's a smash.
reviews.author: Kevin Maher

reviews.text: This is a touching, refreshing, hilarious and lovely film. See it immediately.
reviews.author: Jamie East

reviews.text: Feels so true to the realities of modern relationships that even though it's filled with the sort of bizarre true life scenarios that sound contrived in a movie, it's easy to relate to the complications and dilemmas they generate.
reviews.author: Alistair Harkness

reviews.text: The Big Sick is a rom-com that's smarter than most rom-coms, which isn't saying much, admittedly.
reviews.author: Deborah Ross

reviews.text: A hugely enjoyable, lovable comedy.
reviews.author: Peter Bradshaw

reviews.text: The Big Sick finds plots by losing them. That's its genius. One moment we are in an ethnic satire; the next a romcom; the next a hospital comedy-drama. But that's existence.
reviews.author: Nigel Andrews

reviews.text: Despite the aches and creaks in its extremities, The Big Sick is in rude health where it counts.
reviews.author: Robbie Collin

reviews.text: One of the glories of the film is its ability to find comic details in the most bleak and oppressive situations.
reviews.author: Geoffrey Macnab

reviews.text: Working on a script from Nanjiani and Gordon, director Michael Showalter, who helmed the little-seen but funny Hello, My Name Is Doris, goes soft and gentle when most others would go big and loud.
reviews.author: John Lui

reviews.text: Not quite life-or-death viewing, but as good a star vehicle as Nanjiani might have wished for.
reviews.author: Mike McCahill

reviews.text: Mixing a rom-coma into the romcom, this smart, sweet and highly personal love story finds a winning formula.
reviews.author: Kate Stables

reviews.text: Edgy and hilarious, Nanjiani and Gordon's true story of cross-cultural love is a Trump-baiting marvel that's worth the hype.
reviews.author: Jimi Famurewa

reviews.text: The culture-clash comedy plays out with charming, sometimes toe-curling honesty and an acknowledgement of how complicated life can get when expectations weigh heavy and tradition unceremoniously intervenes.
reviews.author: Emma Simmonds

reviews.text: A lovely and most welcomed breathe of fresh air for the romantic comedy genre. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Fico Cangiano

reviews.text: This is a romantic comedy that is not beholden to any formula or any of the tired tropes of this genre. It's main focus is to do justice to a real life romance that seems to have happened only to put on display on the big screen. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Juanma Fernández París

reviews.text: Michael Showalter directs one of the year's best movies. I'm so glad I got to type those words.
reviews.author: Bob Grimm

reviews.text: Plagiarising their real life experiences on the road to romance, Kumail Nanjiani and Emily V. Gordon have written a screenplay that oozes with the black comedy of life, which is of course the good oil of strong comedy.
reviews.author: Andrew L. Urban

reviews.text: It's delicious. A highly entertaining, laugh outlaid film that explores emotions and behaviour and makes us scratch our heads at the complexity of the human condition. Blends humour, pathos, tragedy and fun like a perfect bouquet.
reviews.author: Louise Keller

reviews.text: An entertaining and deeply felt film.
reviews.author: Sr. Rose Pacatte

reviews.text: The Big Sick works because its humor feels effortless and true, and the laughs spring out of genuine tragedy.
reviews.author: Molly Laich

reviews.text: The year's best comedy, an Annie Hall for the age of ISIS.
reviews.author: Rick Kisonak

reviews.text: The Big Sick is funny but not laugh-out-loud hysterical, and it's moving but not enough to bring you to tears.
reviews.author: Chris Bright

reviews.text: The Big Sick is one of the best romantic comedies of our time. A work of 100% sincerity.
reviews.author: Mike McGranaghan

reviews.text: A hilarious and touching romantic comedy that qualifies as one of best films of 2017.
reviews.author: Frederic and Mary Ann Brussat

reviews.text: Having previously helped skewer the American romantic comedy, Michael Showalter has created one of the sweetest, funniest modern examples of the genre.
reviews.author: Josh Slater-Williams

reviews.text: A challenging true relationship story.
reviews.author: Dennis Schwartz

reviews.text: The movie is no fairy tale; it rings sincere because it shows the warts and blemishes that make perfect love nearly impossible, but allows true love to climb its way to the top of relationship mountain.
reviews.author: Bob Bloom

reviews.text: Ramano's character adores his daughter and his wife but tends to ramble on and on about this, that and the other, often to hysterical effect. Hunter's character's intensity is fierce and funny.
reviews.author: Diane Pershing

reviews.text: The all-American The Big Sick is one of the best-edited comedies in memory... Michael Showalter's [movie] that could have sputtered or confounded without the amazing scene-to-scene, shot-to-shot timing of its jokes and sobs.
reviews.author: Ray Pride

reviews.text: Endearing, surprisingly witty romantic comedy...perfect 'date movie.'
reviews.author: Susan Granger

reviews.text: A charming love letter to humor and how it helps us cope with life, sickness and the craziness that is life. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Jorge Rivera Rubio

reviews.text: The Big Sick is a lovely film, at once familiar and unique in its story of relationships and family and the membranes that can separate us or which we create to isolate ourselves.
reviews.author: Brooke Corso

reviews.text: The film earns its silly and sweet moments just as much as all of the serious. It deserves to be the surprise hit of the summer, which it's on its way to being.
reviews.author: Matthew Passantino

reviews.text: And now I've found the romantic comedy of the summer and perhaps the year.
reviews.author: Kristian M. Lin

reviews.text: Rich in emotional honesty and equal parts funny/moving, The Big Sick successfully infuses the traditional rom-com formula with a modern sensibility.
reviews.author: Sandy Schaefer

reviews.text: At 119 minutes long, it may be too much of a good thing-I have rarely been so aggravated by such a funny and heartwarming film.
reviews.author: Daniel Barnes

reviews.text: It is first and foremost a romantic comedy, one that should be enjoyable regardless of your political views. Hysterical, heartbreaking and ultimately heartwarming, you'd be hard-pressed not to fall in love with The Big Sick.
reviews.author: Matt Hanson

reviews.text: The Big Sick turns out to be more than a boy-meets-girl tale. The story that announces itself as an interfaith, interracial romance turns out to be an intergenerational -- and healing -- one as well.
reviews.author: Carrie Rickey

reviews.text: The Big Sick is a comedy with real meat and meaning, something that's been lacking from the genre in recent years.
reviews.author: Abby Olcese

reviews.text: It's taken a while, but we finally have the first great comedy of 2017 in The Big Sick.
reviews.author: Brad Keefe

reviews.text: It's funny, touching, and perceptive.
reviews.author: James Berardinelli

reviews.text: On paper, it sounds over-the-top wacky and saccharine, but The Big Sick treats its subject matter seriously and mines humor from the characters realistically reacting to awkward and extreme situations.
reviews.author: Stephen Danay

reviews.text: 'The Big Sick,' a sweet little romantic comedy, might ease what ails you from other recent movie-going experiences.
reviews.author: John Urbancich

reviews.text: A feel-great legit Oscar contender and one of 2017's most heartfelt and enjoyable efforts.
reviews.author: Jeffrey Lyles

reviews.text: You'll leave the theatre with a smile on your face. And that's a pretty nice feeling.
reviews.author: Jill Wilson

reviews.text: The most romantic comedy so far this year.
reviews.author: Annlee Ellingson

reviews.text: The Big Sick is a healthy breath of fresh air.
reviews.author: Frank Wilkins

reviews.text: The Big Sick is a sweet film, even with some rough edges, and it will be fun to see more from Nanjiani in the future.
reviews.author: Josh Terry

reviews.text: Turning your own life into material for a show is the most stand-up thing in the world, but it's seldom done as skillfully as in this film.
reviews.author: Sarah Boslaugh

reviews.text: We know where things are going. But frankly, we know where most movies are going. It's how it gets there, and the company we get to keep along the way, that makes "The Big Sick" such a winner.
reviews.author: Rob Thomas

reviews.text: The material may be at the sitcom level, but watching these performers play off each other is pure pleasure.
reviews.author: Robert Horton

reviews.text: "The Big Sick" has a big heart and shows there are still corners left to explore in romantic comedies; it just takes someone willing to find them.
reviews.author: Adam Graham

reviews.text: See it now, don't wait for it to become a cable TV series. A comatose love interest is definitely anti-episodic.
reviews.author: Kelly Vance

reviews.text: Where some movies would just settle for some good laughs, this one does that and warms the heart, too.
reviews.author: Sean P. Means

reviews.text: "The Big Sick" has a lot of charm.
reviews.author: Calvin Wilson

reviews.text: Kumail Nanjiani's autobiographical love story has a fantastic hook but its mild demeanor keeps the comedy from having quite the right sting.
reviews.author: Chris Barsanti

reviews.text: All the characters are flawed but sympathetic-the film has a true generosity of spirit.
reviews.author: Max Weiss

reviews.text: It's hard to overstate just how effectively "The Big Sick" balances its romantic inclinations against life-or-death drama, or how its comedy co-exists with potential heartbreak.
reviews.author: Robert W. Butler

reviews.text: It delivers a real love story with real humor from real people, and the movies can always use more of those.
reviews.author: Josh Bell

reviews.text: Mostly, the movie works for the reason that all the best rom-coms do: you fall in love, a little bit, with Kumail and Emily, and want them to stay together.
reviews.author: Moira MacDonald

reviews.text: All of the thoughtful characters missing from the last ten comedies you've seen? They're here.
reviews.author: Gary Thompson

reviews.text: Kumail Nanjiani's performance can't be undervalued... The comic had to sell us every single piece of the puzzle to take us to a tender place. We had to buy his performance without feeling the sheen of revisionism.
reviews.author: Katherine Monk

reviews.text: "The Big Sick" suffers from an excess of pleasantness, and this very pleasantness thins out its substance, blands out its tone, weakens its comedy.
reviews.author: Richard Brody

reviews.text: Human and humane, it is sweet without being saccharine, funny without becoming raucous, and touching without degenerating into mawkishness-the rare rom-com that appeals to your intelligence rather than insulting it.
reviews.author: Frank Swietek

reviews.text: It helps that the story is a true original - one that you have to really see to believe.
reviews.author: Dana Barbuto

reviews.text: Wickedly funny, this is a film that does not shy away from conflict and heartbreak, but it also finds the reason that love is worth going through it all.
reviews.author: Andrea Chase

reviews.text: Heartwarming, compassionate and wholly human, The Big Sick is highly recommended.
reviews.author: Rashid Irani

reviews.text: While Nanjiani often rambles off during his stand-up routines in the film, his deadpan comedy is at home in the movie, elevating it during its several uncomfortable interactions.
reviews.author: Meher Manda

reviews.text: All the best romantic comedies get even better upon repeat viewings. I'm fully confident The Big Sick will pass that test the next time I see it, which will be very soon.
reviews.author: Richard Roeper

reviews.text: Yes, The Big Sick is a comedy, but it's a comedy that offers up about a million reasons to cry.
reviews.author: Angie Han

reviews.text: It's a slightly messy, often funny and humanity-filled alternative to summer blockbusters.
reviews.author: Anita Katz

reviews.text: Kumail Nanjiani and Emily V. Gordon have told their own story in a funny, highly engaging way that doesn't feel precious or sanitized, but instead is relatable and engrossing from start to finish. And you'll laugh a hell of a lot.
reviews.author: Eric Goldman

reviews.text: With director Michael Showalter's assured comic tone, The Big Sick rates as a fearless and fearlessly funny look at how cultural collisions can end happily.
reviews.author: Stephen Schaefer

reviews.text: Where the film comes up short is in the character of Emily herself, Zoe Kazan's open and quick-witted Emily becoming infantalized during her illness and recovery.
reviews.author: Laura Clifford

reviews.text: This heartfelt and frequently hilarious comedy provides a vibrant and life-affirming twist on familiar themes about immigration, cultural traditions, romantic entanglements and fledgling comedians.
reviews.author: Todd Jorgenson

reviews.text: The best and most original romantic comedy of the year. (Full Content Review for Parents - Sexual Content, Profanity, etc. - also Available)
reviews.author: Jim Judy

reviews.text: Like all Judd Apatow-supervised productions, it's about 10 minutes too long, but that is a small complaint when weighed against Nanjiani and Co.'s remarkable achievement.
reviews.author: Barry Hertz

reviews.text: The Big Sick stands out among the usual rom-com fare, and not just because of the cultural flavours of its lead
reviews.author: Radheyan Simonpillai

reviews.text: It's all very naturalistic, funny and surprising, all the more so for not taking the easy path of milking the stand-up scenes for laughs.
reviews.author: Chris Knight

reviews.text: [Nanjiani and Gordon have] written a comedy that, yes, does recognize the seriousness of the situation but also focuses on the uncomfortable, awkward, and difficult nature of it, too.
reviews.author: Mark Dujsik

reviews.text: The movie chugs along on the chemistry between Nanjiani, acquitting himself well as a droll leading man, and Zoe Kazan as his sunny, devoted sweetheart, though they're completely upstaged by Holly Hunter and Ray Romano as the girlfriend's parents
reviews.author: J. R. Jones

reviews.text: Hilarious and heartbreaking with no clear trajectory, frequently catching viewers off guard, it's a rom-com of both heart and brain about a couple tested by illness and clashing cultures.
reviews.author: Peter Howell

reviews.text: The Big Sick is as personal as it gets, but Gordon and Nanjiani pull no punches and steer well clear of preciousness. I laughed plenty at their film, cried my guts out, too, and went home elated.
reviews.author: Kimberley Jones

reviews.text: It's a movie that not only puts human imperfections and incongruities on display, but also revels in them.
reviews.author: Ann Hornaday

reviews.text: The movie treats the people on screen generously, and it's a romantic comedy with surprising depth of feeling, glancing on all sorts of things: race, religion, tolerance, understanding, the competitive peculiarity of stand-up comedy ...
reviews.author: Michael Phillips

reviews.text: There are a lot of reasons to love "The Big Sick," in addition to its intelligence and complex characters. It's hilarious, from start to finish.
reviews.author: Chris Hewitt

reviews.text: You don't have to hole up at home praying to the Netflix, Amazon and Hulu gods for cinematic salvation until the fall. Case in point: "The Big Sick," a small movie that makes a big impact.
reviews.author: Cary Darling

reviews.text: I love "The Big Sick."
reviews.author: Bill Goodykoontz

reviews.text: With his welcome appearance at the top of the bill, Silicon Valley's Kumail Nanjiani is just one of the good reasons to catch this summer charmer.
reviews.author: Adrian Mack

reviews.text: Despite its pandemic-sounding title, The Big Sick delivers a fresh, funny, endearing and surprisingly emotional story of romance and survival, not necessarily in that order.
reviews.author: Dann Gire

reviews.text: Nanjiani and Gordon having difficulty managing the nuance of their story and the needs of mainstream cinema. They come up with a picture that has a defined cultural perspective, but remains bland overall.
reviews.author: Brian Orndorf

reviews.text: "The Big Sick," with ease and seeming effortlessness, makes us care a lot of about these people, together and separately. And their journey is odd enough to be interesting.
reviews.author: Mick LaSalle

reviews.text: Functions...not only as a boilerplate rom-com that's consistently amusing and possessed with charming leads, but also as a heartwarming drama.
reviews.author: Peter Canavese

reviews.text: I could talk about this movie and their story for hours, but I'll leave it at this: please go see The Big Sick.
reviews.author: Akemi Aiello

reviews.text: One of the best romantic comedies to hit theaters in a decade.
reviews.author: Rick Bentley

reviews.text: The recent death of the American rom-com has been much remarked upon, but it only takes one great film to zap it back into life. The Big Sick just might be that film.
reviews.author: David Sims

reviews.text: It's a wildly different experience and the fact that it's true makes "The Big Sick" even more unique.
reviews.author: Jeanne Kaplan

reviews.text: Excellent writing, superb acting, expert direction, and more --- it is easily one of the best films of this, or any other, year.
reviews.author: David Kaplan

reviews.text: It's painstakingly authentic in its evocation of what sometimes feels like the entire conceivable range of emotions. That's because Nanjiani... and Gordon are sharp writers with a knack for underpinning deadpan dialogue with understated emotions.
reviews.author: Robert Levin

reviews.text: The often slick, just occasionally slack Sick is first and foremost an autobiography, and while it's been designed to deliver maximum laughs and emotion, a quirky authenticity hovers over even its most manipulative moments.
reviews.author: Bob Strauss

reviews.text: Those are a lot of plates for any film to keep spinning, and while it isn't always a complete success - it could stand to lose 15 or 20 minutes - it's the kind of sweetly funny movie love story that's so bizarre that it has to be real.
reviews.author: Alonso Duralde

reviews.text: There is comic gold in the cultural disconnect between Kumail and Emily's congenial, if politically incorrect, father.
reviews.author: Zach Schonfeld

reviews.text: To call The Big Sick the best comedy so far this year is to skimp its appeal. It's a very funny movie with a surprising amount of depth, and somehow the jokes and the seriousness heighten each other.
reviews.author: Peter Rainer

reviews.text: Thoughtful romantic dramedy has swearing, drinking, sex.
reviews.author: Betsy Bozdech

reviews.text: Easily the best rom-com of 2017, so far, and one of the most touching and daring in years, too.
reviews.author: Gregory Wakeman

reviews.text: Nanjiani's face has an Old Hollywood repose, but his eyes can melt into pools of concern with barely a flicker of transition.
reviews.author: Kurt Loder

reviews.text: Smart, funny, touching, heartfelt.
reviews.author: Nell Minow

reviews.text: The Big Sick is bracingly funny, heartrending, and intelligent, a perfect alternative to the pirates, mummies, and other creatures inhabiting multiplexes this summer. No wonder it was the runaway hit of this year's Sundance Film Festival.
reviews.author: Leonard Maltin

reviews.text: Anyone who's dealt with an extended hospital stay on either side will relate to this. Hopefully people who have been fortunate enough not to spend time in a hospital will be able to relate to what it's like just waiting, not knowing, not being told.
reviews.author: Fred Topel

reviews.text: The Big Sick can sometimes be awfully conventional, but among its key assets is its radiant view of its characters.
reviews.author: Tim Grierson

reviews.text: Movie characters spend more time lounging around hospitals than pharmacy reps, but The Big Sick is the first "hospital film" in a while that makes us feel the stakes of a vicious mystery disease in our guts.
reviews.author: Andrew Lapin

reviews.text: It's a lot for any movie to take on. The Big Sick pulls it off with unquenchable humor and ineffable grace.
reviews.author: Joe Morgenstern

reviews.text: There are some sweet early scenes establishing the characters' rapport... but Gordon and Nanjiani are so enamored of the standup-comedy world that it takes nearly 40 minutes for an actual conflict to be brought up.
reviews.author: Kyle Smith

reviews.text: Tore than a love story, this is a story about Kumail's relationship with two sets of parents, his own and Emily's -- and both are full of conflicts that range from hilarious to frustrating to incredibly sweet.
reviews.author: Erika W. Smith

reviews.text: Invigorates the Apatovian formula and indeed an entire genre with a thorny study of interracial relationships and the bonds that hold immigrant families together across an ever-widening generation gap.
reviews.author: Justin Chang

reviews.text: Nanjiani and Gordon are reluctant to paint themselves or their families in broad strikes, each character a dysfunctional maelstrom of good and bad, and it's this genuine fact-based texture that helps to make the film feel far from a Hollywood construct.
reviews.author: Benjamin Lee

reviews.text: This is an impressive first feature, one that resonates more strongly thanks to its fact-based underpinnings.
reviews.author: Brian Lowry

reviews.text: What The Big Sick gets at, in its obvious but necessary manner, is how America undermines traditions from other countries, and always has.
reviews.author: John Anderson

reviews.text: "Authentic" is an overused word in movie reviews, but there's no better way to describe The Big Sick: Every inch of it feels true, and not just because it's drawn from real life.
reviews.author: Alissa Wilkinson

reviews.text: Again and again, [Showalter] finds that laughter-through-tears sweet spot, often in the unlikeliest of places.
reviews.author: Christy Lemire

reviews.text: A joyous, generous-hearted romantic comedy that, even as it veers into difficult terrain, insists that we just need to keep on laughing.
reviews.author: Manohla Dargis

reviews.text: It's an exceedingly high degree of difficulty to hit the perfect chord of humor and heart, plucking the heartstrings just so, blending laughter and tears, and "The Big Sick" strums them just right.
reviews.author: Katie Walsh

reviews.text: A cross cultural romance with surprising twists and turns makes for great comedy AND great drama . Kumail Nanjiani's true life tale is one not to miss.
reviews.author: Pete Hammond

reviews.text: Comic Kumail Nanjiani and his wife/co-screenwriter Emily V. Gordon carve this heartfelt love story out of her health crisis and their own culture-clash relationship. Not just the funniest romcom in ages, it's one of 2017's best films.
reviews.author: Peter Travers

reviews.text: This is a comedy that needs room to breathe, that would feel gutted if it ran a mere hour-and-a-half - the same way an epic trimmed of an hour by nervous studio execs would seem gutted.
reviews.author: Matt Prigge

reviews.text: The Big Sick becomes a story rarely explored or romanticized on film, about what it's like to bond with the parents of the person you're in love with.
reviews.author: Emily Yoshida

reviews.text: It's cute, funny, and vulnerable, The rest of the world is finally catching up to crushing on Nanjiani and Gordon.
reviews.author: Kristy Puchko

reviews.text: Some stories are too good to be true, and some true stories are too good for the movies. Luckily for us, The Big Sick is neither.
reviews.author: Lindsey Bahr

reviews.text: In his first starring role, co-writer Kumail Nanjiani delivers a crowd-pleaser with this semi-autobiographical rom-com/culture-clash dramedy.
reviews.author: Kevin Lally

reviews.text: Hating on this sweetheart of a rom-com must be the cinematic equivalent of kicking a puppy.
reviews.author: Joanna Langfield

reviews.text: Michael Showalter's The Big Sick puts a thoughtful spin on the rom-com, though maybe it's more accurate to call the film a rom-com interrupted.
reviews.author: Peter Goldberg

reviews.text: The Big Sick is less a bitter pill and more a genuine story about love, individuality and - biggest of all - life's beautiful imperfections.
reviews.author: Matt Donato

reviews.text: It's a winning and genuinely funny rom-com that proves there's more than one way to a heart-swelling happily ever after. Call it The Big Crowd Pleaser.
reviews.author: Mara Reinstein

reviews.text: Deft and appealing ...
reviews.author: Anthony Lane

reviews.text: Kumail Nanjiani co-writes and stars in a refreshing movie that recasts what the romantic male lead looks like
reviews.author: Candice Frederick

reviews.text: Though a drama about a serious subject, this is the year's funniest movie to date.
reviews.author: Harvey S. Karten

reviews.text: "The Big Sick" definitely gets extra points for its real-life factor.
reviews.author: Jeffrey M. Anderson

reviews.text: This movie keeps a lot of balls in the air: generational and cultural conflict, hospital drama, screwball banter-and only rarely lets one drop.
reviews.author: Dana Stevens

reviews.text: It is nice to finally see a romantic comedy that isn't afraid to tackle dark subject matters in a mature way.
reviews.author: Scott Menzel

reviews.text: The love story is messy, complicated, yet unconsciously romantic.
reviews.author: Jacqueline Coley

reviews.text: Thanks to Nanjiani and Gordon's script-equally funny, frank, and frightening-The Big Sick emerges as an unshakeable comedy made by, and for, a generation rediscovering what intimacy means.
reviews.author: Paula Mejía

reviews.text: Each of the characters here, presumably because they are rooted in truth, is given room to breathe and shows an ability to be changed by circumstance.
reviews.author: Amber Wilkinson

reviews.text: It's the best kind of romantic comedy, small in scope but vast in impact, and a reminder of just how great the genre can be when we give it the chance.
reviews.author: Meredith Borders

reviews.text: The movie's so good... in part because of the degree to which it considers marriage not just as a relationship between two people but between two families.
reviews.author: Alison Willmore

reviews.text: This isn't a *bad* movie per se, but it is an extremely frustrating one that left me longing for the days when rom-coms weren't structured like The Return Of The King.
reviews.author: Sean Burns

reviews.text: Already, The Big Sick is scoring points on familiar rom-com territory, so when it suddenly morphs into a completely different film -- a bracingly sophisticated one -- you'll want to cry with happiness. (The real tears will come soon enough.)
reviews.author: Joshua Rothkopf

reviews.text: The film is very charming and never loses its humor even when being mixed with drama.
reviews.author: Yasmin Kleinbart

reviews.text: Its authenticity and candor is part of what makes 'The Big Sick' shine so brightly - it's got the lived-in coziness and complicated wit of a James L. Brooks movie. But, y'know, one of the good ones, like 'Terms of Endearment' or 'Broadcast News.'
reviews.author: Jason Bailey

reviews.text: Infused with honesty and authenticity, Michael Showalter's crowd-pleaser is an instantly winning heart-stealer and a superbly well-timed story of culture clash that resolves into a lovely tale of mutual understanding and acceptance.
reviews.author: Tomris Laffly

reviews.text: Comedian and actor Kumail Nanjiani and writer Emily V. Gordon mine their personal history for laughs, heartache, and hard-earned insight in The Big Sick, a film that's by turns romantic, rueful, and hilarious.
reviews.author: Geoff Berkshire

reviews.text: A deserved leading man turn for Silicon Valley" star Kumail Nanjiani.
reviews.author: Matt Donnelly

reviews.text: While James L. Brooks is a good point of comparison, as is producer Judd Apatow's talky, hangout-centric approach, Showalter has made something unique and wonderful here.
reviews.author: Dominick Suzanne-Mayer

reviews.text: It offers us not a sickness, but a cure for what ails our weary hearts.
reviews.author: Neil Miller

reviews.text: The Big Sick doesn't need resuscitation from cheap jokes; its strength comes from a deeper place.
reviews.author: Jordan Hoffman

reviews.text: Nanjiani and Showalter imbue the film with so much more character-based truth than we usually see from the genre. It's the best romantic comedy in years.
reviews.author: Brian Tallerico

reviews.text: As Emily, Kazan is fantastic, unselfconscious and deadpan, a welcome respite from typical romcom leads so often preoccupied with sorting out the rules of dating.
reviews.author: Elena Razlogova

reviews.text: A beautiful, somewhat traditional love story.
reviews.author: Chris Plante

reviews.text: In every conceivable way is this film a crowd-pleaser, pushing you to laugh and laugh until you cry.
reviews.author: Dan Mecca

reviews.text: So well acted and dense with insights into the culture clash at its center that nothing about the central dynamic is strained.
reviews.author: Eric Kohn

reviews.text: The Big Sick is the complete package. An ecstatic romantic vision, unafraid of dangerous comedy, that earns all the laughs and misty eyes it goes for. Modern romantic comedies now have a standard to live up to.
reviews.author: Scott Beggs

reviews.text: A star-making comedy for Kumail Nanjiani.
reviews.author: Chris Bumbray

reviews.text: An intensely personal film, a triumph for Kumail Nanjiani, and one of the most hilarious and personal films this year.
reviews.author: Nathan McVay

reviews.text: 'The Big Sick' is hilarious, surprisingly emotional, and it has a big heart. I can't wait to see it again.
reviews.author: Matt Goldberg

reviews.text: The Big Sick is an enormous crowdpleaser, funny and touching in about equal measure, built atop an intense experience, and wise about the ways we interact with both our own parents and those of the people we date.
reviews.author: A.A. Dowd

reviews.text: Zoe Kazan can transform even the most stock role into something indelible.
reviews.author: Noel Murray

reviews.text: It's all at once a movie about overcoming disease, a story about cultural assimilation, a movie about stand-up comedians, a coming of age tale, and a rom-com. On the surface it shouldn't work at all.
reviews.author: Travis Hopson

reviews.text: Almost every romantic comedy is predicated on artificiality. The Big Sick is authentic from start to finish.
reviews.author: Matt Singer

reviews.text: Just like Trainwreck elevated Amy Schumer to being a household name, The Big Sick really could do the same for Kumail Nanjiani.
reviews.author: Mike Ryan

reviews.text: This is a carefully-crafted comedy which can withstand the tonal shifts.
reviews.author: Fionnuala Halligan

reviews.text: A funny and tender drawn-from-life love story.
reviews.author: John DeFore

synopsis: Kumail is a Pakistani comic, who meets an American graduate student named Emily at one of his stand-up shows. As their relationship blossoms, he soon becomes worried about what his traditional Muslim parents will think of her. When Emily suddenly comes down with an illness that leaves her in a coma, Kumail finds himself developing a bond with her deeply concerned mother and father.
